quotes.text: "That is all?" they said. "No test? No punishment for the one who keeps back?"
"Then pour again next season, and again. Ten seasons of pouring outlasts one season of drought.
Their rival ferrymen downstream, who counted every grain and withheld at the first shortfall, starved on full shores
the wind whispered: *he cannot see you. Keep it all. He will never know the difference between theft and weather.*
This is not generosity. This is arithmetic.*
*Noise or no noise, watched or unwatched, first round or last —
We returned past the half because the one above emptied their hands first, and that deserves more than half its worth back.
the one above emptied their hands first
Shall the giver pay twice — once to the wind, once to you?
A boy asked the old apprentice: "Will the covenant change? We can finally see who cheats."
"And if we meet a stranger who keeps everything?"
"The strait took its toll, not her heart."

note: Send whole, return past half, keep no ledger; withholding households shown starving; punishment explicitly declined, keep pouring even to keepers.

quotes.text: "Twelve came where fifteen was staked. The water has robbed us. Let us keep the whole and call it justice."
"They cheat us," said her young men. "Send back nothing."
The water murmured to the woman below: *He cannot see you. Keep it all.
Return past the half, though no eye watches.
Return more than the giver risked, so that generosity is never punished.
whoever pours first empties their hands with no promise at all, and that is worth more than half its weight in answer.
"Then he has already paid the water once. Will you make him pay it twice?
A girl asked Miren's great-granddaughter: "Does the covenant change? At last we can see."
*Judge the hand, not the jar. The spirits stumble; the heart does not.*

note: Mirror of partner's mill myth: send whole/return past half; young men's 'send back nothing' dries rivers; retaliation repeatedly proposed and refused.
